title: Equations and Inequalities
mcqIntro: Twelve questions on the six kinds of equation this chapter solves and on the three ways an inequality's answer has to be written. Each wrong option is a real mistake with a name; the feedback tells you which one you made.

mcq.stem: Solving $4(3x-2)=12x-8$ collapses to the line $-8=-8$. What does that tell you about the equation?

options.a: The only solution is $x=0$, because $x$ disappeared
options.b: It is a contradiction, so it has no solution at all
options.c: It is an identity, so every real number is a solution
options.d: The only solution is $x=-8$, read off the last line

mcq.stem: Why must every candidate solution of a rational equation be checked in the **original** equation?

options.a: Because the LCD is easy to get wrong when a denominator is unfactored
options.b: Because dividing both sides by a variable can quietly delete a root
options.c: Because the distributive property does not apply to fractional terms
options.d: Because multiplying by the LCD can produce a root that makes a denominator zero

mcq.stem: Solve $\lvert 3x-6\rvert>9$. Which is the solution set?
A student solves $x(x+4)=5$ by writing "$x=5$ or $x+4=5$". What is the mistake?

options.a: The zero product property works only when the product equals zero
options.b: The two factors must be multiplied out before they can be split
options.c: Both sides of the equation should have been divided by $x$ first
options.d: The square root property was the method this equation needed

mcq.stem: What does the discriminant of $4x^{2}-12x+9=0$ tell you?

options.a: There are two distinct real solutions
options.d: There is one real and one nonreal solution

mcq.stem: The two legs of a right triangle are $3$ cm and $6$ cm shorter than the hypotenuse $x$. Which equation models the triangle?
Squaring both sides of $\sqrt{x+3}=x-3$ produces the candidates $x=1$ and $x=6$. Which of them actually solve the original equation?

options.c: No value satisfies the original equation

mcq.stem: Which pair of equations is equivalent to $\lvert 2x-1\rvert=\lvert x+4\rvert$?
A compound inequality has the solution "$x\le 2$ **or** $x\ge 7$". Which is that set in interval notation?
Modelling a rectangle gives $w^{2}+6w-40=0$, where $w$ is its width in metres. What is the width?

short.prompt: Solve $\dfrac{2x-1}{3}-\dfrac{x+4}{6}=\dfrac12$. Show the step that clears the fractions.
Solve $\dfrac{3}{x-4}+2=\dfrac{x-1}{x-4}$. State the restriction before you solve, and give the solution set.
Simplify $\sqrt{-8}\cdot\sqrt{-2}$ and $i^{-22}$. For the first, say in one sentence why $\sqrt{a}\sqrt{b}=\sqrt{ab}$ may not be used.
Solve $3x^{2}-2x-4=0$ using the quadratic formula. Give the exact solutions, fully simplified.
Solve $2x^{2}-6x+5=0$, and say what the discriminant predicted before you solved it.
A rectangular garden is $4$ m longer than it is wide and covers $96\ \text{m}^{2}$. Find its dimensions, and say why one root of your equation is discarded.
Solve $\sqrt{3x+7}-1=x$. Give the solution set and show the check that decides it.
Solve $-1\le\dfrac{3-2x}{4}<2$. Describe the graph, then write the solution set in set-builder notation and in interval notation.
